paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. Jesus says the Son of Man will come in a cloud "with power and great glory" (Luke 21:27). While the nations are bewildered and men faint from fear, Jesus tells His listeners, "stand up and lift up your heads, because your redemption is drawing near" (Luke 21:28). The same moment that sends some people to the floor is the one He says to face with your chin UP.

So how do you get ready? Jesus gives a parable about the fig tree and all the trees: when they sprout leaves, you know summer is near (Luke 21:29-31). Then He warns that hearts can get "weighed down by dissipation, drunkenness, and the worries of life" (Luke 21:34). I think that's the sneaky one, friend, because worries don't feel like a danger. They feel like Tuesday. He says "keep watch at all times, and pray that you may have the strength to escape all that is about to happen and to stand before the Son of Man" (Luke 21:36).

Here's what holds it all up: "Heaven and earth will pass away, but My words will never pass away" (Luke 21:33). That's why my ovens stay ready, baker. I don't know the day, and Jesus says it will come "upon all who dwell on the face of all the earth" (Luke 21:35), so this word is for you too. Keep your eyes up, keep your heart light, and keep praying. And the story isn't over, because the Gospel of Luke keeps going.
